input.quote: (d) Termination for Competing Product of Sanofi. If after [***]: (i) Sanofi or its Affiliates, alone or with or through a Third Party, develop, manufacture or commercialize a Competing Product and (ii) Sanofi or its Affiliates have not commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product prior to commencing the activities in Section 12.2(d)(i), RevMed may terminate this Agreement effective [***] after it delivers written notice to Sanofi that it is exercising its rights under this Section 12.2(d)
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Sanofi, so the preferred position is met. Sanofi's licence is in the "Field", defined as "any and all uses" (§1.36), and no covenant anywhere prohibits or limits Sanofi (or its Affiliates) from researching, developing, manufacturing, acquiring or commercialising competing or other products: Articles III, XIII (13.3 and mutual covenants 13.4) and XV contain no such undertaking. The only exclusivity covenant runs the other way and benefits us — §3.5(a) bars RevMed and its Affiliates from working on SHP2 Inhibitor products outside the Collaboration. Section 12.2(d) is a RevMed termination right triggered by Sanofi's Competing Product activity (with a cure election available to Sanofi), not a restrictive covenant: Sanofi remains free to pursue a Competing Product, and the consequence is termination of this collaboration with the effects in §12.3(c) (p0500), which is a termination mechanic reviewed under the termination rules, not a restriction on the businesses we may operate. Likewise, the §15.2 change-of-control conditions at p0614 (separation of Competing Products of the Acquiror Family, no Know-How exchange) are mutual conditions on assignment/CoC treatment of IP, not a prohibition on Sanofi's own or an acquirer's competing programmes. We note only that "Competing Product" (§1.20) is partly redacted, so its precise criteria should be confirmed; on its face it is limited by reference to defined criteria and excludes Products. No redline is warranted.
